title: SAP SUIM: user information system
tags: sap, suim, user, role, authorization, audit
excerpt: Reports para auditoría de usuarios, roles y autorizaciones.
body:
## Uso
`SUIM` → árbol de reports agrupados:
- **User** — queries sobre usuarios
- **Roles** — sobre roles
- **Profiles** — sobre profiles
- **Authorizations**
- **Change documents** — histórico de cambios
- **Comparisons** — comparar auth entre users

## Reports útiles

### Users by complex criteria
`SUIM → User → Users by Complex Selection Criteria` (`RSUSR002`):
Filtros combinables:
- Locked / valid dates
- User group
- Role assignment
- Authorization object + values
- Last logon date

Ejemplo: 'Users con role SAP_ALL y last logon >6 meses' → export → alert compliance.

### Users by role
`Users → Users by Role`:
List users que tienen un role específico. Útil para ver 'quién tiene SAP_ADMIN'.

### Roles by user
`Roles → Roles by User Assignment`:
Dado un user, lista sus roles.

### Roles by authorization
`Roles → Roles by Complex Selection Criteria`:
List roles que contienen un auth object específico.

## Change documents (audit)
`SUIM → Change documents`:
- **For Users** — cambios en users
- **For Profiles** — cambios en profiles
- **For Roles** — cambios en roles
- **For Auth Objects** — cambios en auth objects (dev)

Por fecha + user modificador. Crítico para auditorías.

## Comparaciones
`SUIM → Comparisons`:
- **Users → Users**: comparar 2 users, ver diferencias
- **Roles → Roles**: comparar 2 roles
- **Auth Values → Auth Values**

Útil para: 'copiar auth de user A a user B'.

## Reports SoD (Segregation of Duties)
Business user típicamente NO debe tener:
- Create PO + Post GR + Post IR (mismo user hace todo el ciclo = fraud risk)
- Post FI + Approve payment
- User admin + Auditor

SUIM ayuda con:
- Users by combination of transactions
- Roles by combination of authorizations

Algunas compañías compran GRC (Governance Risk Compliance) para SoD automatizado.

## Report authorization checks
`Roles → by Auth Value in Trace`:
Habilitar trace en ST01 → correr transacción → SUIM ve qué roles proveen las auth necesarias.

## Export
Cada report → **List** → **Export** → Excel/CSV.

## Autorización
- `S_USER_SAS` — access SUIM
- `S_USER_AUT` — auth data queries
- `S_USER_AGR` — role data

## Common queries mensuales

### Users nuevos
Date range: último mes
Criteria: Created after < date >

### Users con SAP_ALL
Role = SAP_ALL → list users.
Deben ser <5 y solo emergencias.

### Roles sin usuarios
`Roles → Roles by Complex Selection Criteria` → 'User assignment: no users'.
Roles huérfanos → limpiar.

### Passwords weak (in local systems only)
`Users → with initial password` — users con contraseña initial (nunca cambiada).

## SUIM combinado con SM19/SM20
SUIM: quién TIENE permisos.
SM19/SM20: quién USA permisos (audit log de accesos).

title: SAP SM19/SM20: security audit log
tags: sap, sm19, sm20, security, audit, logon
excerpt: Habilitar y consultar audit log de eventos sensibles.
body:
## Habilitar audit log (SM19)
`SM19` → **Configuration** → tabs por client:
- Client (100, 200, etc.)
- User group
- **Event definitions**: qué auditar

### Categorías de eventos
- **Logon/Logoff**
- **Transaction start**
- **RFC**
- **Report start**
- **User master changes**
- **System events**

### Ejemplo config
Para PRD, típico enable:
- **AU1**: successful logon
- **AU2**: failed logon
- **AU3**: user locked
- **AUA**: report start
- **AUE**: RFC/CPIC login

## Activate
Select config → **Save** → **Activate** el filter.

Cambios requieren restart del app server para tomar efecto (aunque parte se aplica dinámicamente).

## Ver eventos (SM20)
`SM20` → selection:
- **User**
- **Date/time**
- **Class** (categoría)
- **Terminal**
- **Client**

Execute → ALV con eventos:
- Timestamp
- User
- Terminal (IP / hostname)
- Class + Event
- Message

## Filtros útiles

### Failed logins del último día
Class = **AU2** (failed logon).

### User cambiado por admin
SM20 → User = `<user>` → Class = **AU5** (user master change).

### Access a transaction sensible
SM20 → Message text contains `SU01` (o whichever).

### Login fuera de hours
SM20 → date range → filter by time of day → identificar logins nocturnos anómalos.

## Export para SIEM externo
**List** → **Export** → CSV → alimentar SIEM (Splunk, Sentinel).

## Retention
Default: audit files locales por app server, ~1-3 meses (según config).

### File location
```
/usr/sap/<SID>/<INSTANCE>/log/audit_<date>
```

### Retention parameters
```
rsau/max_diskspace/local        # per-server
rsau/max_diskspace/central      # central si configurado
```

### Central audit log server
Para compliance: forward audit logs a un central server (o SIEM external).

Config con parameter `rsau/dsp/central_audit_active`.

## Filters en runtime (sin restart)
SM19 → **Dynamic Configuration**:
- Habilitar filters temporariamente para audit especial
- Sin restart

## Real-time monitoring
SM20 con option 'Statistical analysis' — dashboard con stats:
- Failed logins por hora
- Users con más failed attempts
- Transactions más accedidas

## Alertas
SM19 puede triggear alertas en RZ20 CCMS:
- Auth object protection
- Notification method configurable

## Compliance
### GDPR / ISO 27001
Requieren audit trail de:
- Accesos a datos personales
- Cambios en master data
- Login attempts

**SAP audit log es la fuente primaria**.

## Autorización
- `S_TCODE = SM19, SM20`
- `S_ADMI_FCD = AUDD` — audit log admin

Restringir a security team only. Users normales no deben poder ver quién más entró.

title: SAP KE30: report builder de controlling
tags: sap, ke30, co-pa, reports, controlling
excerpt: Reportes de contabilidad de gestión (CO-PA).
body:
## CO-PA (Profitability Analysis)
Módulo de Controlling para análisis de rentabilidad por dimensión (product, customer, region).

## Uso
`KE30` → seleccionar report existente → **Execute**.

### Ejemplos de reports pre-built
- Sales revenue by customer
- Contribution margin by product
- Actual vs. plan variance
- Regional profitability

### Selection screen
- **Fiscal year**
- **Period range**
- **Company code**
- **Version** (0 = actual, 100+ = planning)
- Otros filtros según report (customer group, product hierarchy, etc.)

## Ejecutar
F8 → resultados en list format.

### Interacción
- **Drill down** — click en un total → break por otra dimensión
- **Navigation attributes**: swap dimensions (customer ↔ product)
- **Filters**: aplicar dinámicamente
- **Save layout**

## Crear nuevo report
`KE31` → creator wizard:
1. Report name + description
2. Data source: profitability analysis segment (CO-PA)
3. Characteristics (dimensiones): customer, product, sales org
4. Key figures (medidas): revenue, cost, margin
5. Layout (rows/columns)

## KE30 vs KEBC vs S_ALR_*
- `KE30` — CO-PA reports
- `KEBC` — batch execution de CO-PA reports
- `S_ALR_87013611`, etc — standard SAP reports (por transaction) — muchos usan KE30 backend

## Modificar report existente
`KE32` — change report.
O KE31 → 'Copy from existing' → adjust.

## Ver datos raw
`KE24` — CO-PA line items browser (equivalente SE16 for CE1/CE2 tables).

## Access a CO-PA en SE16
Tables:
- `CE1<opCoArea>` — actual data
- `CE2<opCoArea>` — plan data
- `CE3<opCoArea>` — segment level

Ejemplo: CE10000 (para operating concern 0000).

## Autorización
- `K_KEB_TCA` — main auth object
- `K_REPO_CCA` — report groups
- `K_KA09_CCA` — key figure groups

## Performance
CO-PA con años de data + muchos characteristics → puede tardar.

Optimizaciones:
- Aggregate tables
- BW/BW-on-HANA para reporting analítico grande
- Report variants con fecha limitada

## Common issues

### 'No data for selection'
- Client / period equivocado
- Version 0 (actual) vs 1 (plan)
- CO-PA no active para esa combination

### 'Structure XYZ does not match'
- Report fue creado en version diferente
- Regenerate: KE32 → **Extras** → **Regenerate**

### Slow execution
- Verify aggregates en KEDR
- Break selection en múltiples reports más pequeños

## Alternate: SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC)
Modern replacement para KE30 en S/4HANA. Mejor UI/dashboards.

title: SAP KO01/KO02/KO03: internal orders
tags: sap, ko01, ko02, ko03, internal order, co
excerpt: Crear/modificar/ver órdenes internas (CO) para acumular costos.
body:
## Uso
- `KO01` — create
- `KO02` — change
- `KO03` — display

## Contexto
Internal order = 'cost collector' para agrupar costos por proyecto/campaign/evento:
- Campaña de marketing
- Auto de la empresa (accum gastos de mantenimiento)
- Proyecto interno pequeño (grandes → PS module)

## Create (KO01)
1. **Order type**: `Z*` custom o standard como `0100` (internal order overhead)
2. **Order name**: descripción

### Header tabs
- **Assignments**: company code, business area, currency
- **Control data**: order status, statistical (yes/no)
- **Prd-end closing**: settlement rule
- **General data**: person responsible, start/end date
- **Investment**: si es CAPEX (asset under construction)
- **Period-end closing**: settlement

### Settlement rule (tab)
- **Receiver**: dónde van los costs al final (cost center, WBS, asset)
- **%**: distribución si multiple receivers
- **Category**: FUL (full) / PER (por período)

## Release order
Status initial: **CRTD** (created).

Para postear:
KO02 → menu **Order** → **Release** → status → **REL**.

## Postear costos

### FI direct
`FB50` con account assignment → Internal Order = KO number.

### From PO/GR
Purchase requisition o PO con account assignment 'F' (Order) → cost va al KO al momento del GR.

### Time confirmation (services)
`CATS` → time recording → cost center → KO (via activity type).

## Ver costos acumulados
`KOB1` — internal order actual line items (similar a FBL3N pero for KO):
List de todos los postings al KO con detalle.

Or `S_ALR_87013019` — actual/plan comparison.

## Settlement (mensual/trimestral)
`KO88` — actual settlement:
1. KO number + period + fiscal year
2. Processing type: **Test** first (sin postear)
3. Review resultado
4. **Live run** — postea a receivers

Settles los actual costs del período según rule → clears the KO parcial o total.

## Status
- **CRTD** — created (no postings allowed)
- **REL** — released (postings OK)
- **TECO** — technically completed
- **CLSD** — closed (no more postings)

Change status en KO02.

## Reporting
- `S_ALR_87013015` — plan/actual internal order overview
- `S_ALR_87013019` — actual/plan/variance
- `S_ALR_87013016` — order line items

## Errors comunes

### 'Order X does not exist'
- Number range issue
- KO no released
- Verificar en KOK5 (mass processing)

### 'Order is locked'
- Alguien está editando
- KO03 en solo lectura funciona

### 'Cannot post: settlement rule missing'
KO02 → tab Settlement rule → definir receivers antes de postear.

## Ver order group
`KOH1` — group definition (agrupar orders por categoría para reporting).

## Autorización
- `K_ORDER` — internal order object
- `K_CCA` — cost center accounting

## Trans populares related
- `KA01/KA02/KA03` — cost element
- `KS01/KS02/KS03` — cost center
- `KP06` — cost center planning

title: SAP OB08: exchange rates
tags: sap, ob08, exchange rate, currency, tcurr
excerpt: Mantener tipos de cambio para conversión multi-moneda.
body:
## Uso
`OB08` (Transaction Currency: Exchange Rates) → editor de tabla TCURR.

### Filter
- **Exchange rate type** (M = middle rate, most common)
- **From currency**
- **To currency**
- **Valid from** (date)

## Add nueva rate
1. **New Entries**
2. Fill:
   - Exchange rate type: `M`
   - Valid from: `2026-07-01`
   - From: `USD`
   - To: `COP`
   - Ratio (from): `1`
   - Exchange rate: `4200.00`
   - Ratio (to): `1`
3. Save

## Exchange rate types (comunes)
- **M** — middle (average) rate — usado para postings
- **B** — bank buying rate — used for revaluation of receivables (customer)
- **G** — bank selling rate — for payables
- **P** — planning rate — para budget
- **EURX/EURY** — Euro fixed exchange rates

Cada company code define qué rate type usar para posting/valuation.

## Bulk update — script BATCH
`OB08` es tedioso para muchas rates. Alternate:

### Import CSV
`SE38` → programa `RFTBFF00` — importa desde CSV.

### Web service / Cloud
S/4HANA + BTP: integración con Fintech APIs para pull automatic rates diariamente.

### RFC batch
Custom program que pull de banco central + populate TCURR.

## Ver histórico
`OB08` → filter por currency pair → ver todas las rates por fecha.

Or `SE16N` → TCURR → filter.

## Ratio (para monedas grandes)
Algunas monedas usan ratio para precision:
- COP/USD: 1 USD = 4200 COP → ratio 1:1, rate = 4200
- Alternative: rate 42, ratio 1:100 (interpret 42 COP = 100 USD?) — rare

Generalmente ratio 1:1 y rate directo.

## Directional vs both ways
SAP guarda solo UNA dirección (from → to). La inversa se calcula:
`1 / rate = inverse rate`.

O configurar 'Inverse rate calculation allowed' en OY03 (currency table).

## Company code impact
Cada company code (`OB22`) define:
- Local currency (currency 1)
- Second currency (currency 2 — group/parallel)
- Third currency (currency 3)

Postings se convierten to secondary currencies usando OB08 rates.

## Ver conversion en un doc
FB03 → doc → tab **Amount in Local Currency**:
- Local currency: COP (con rate aplicado)
- Doc currency: USD (original)
- Rate: shown

## Errors

### 'Enter rate USD/EUR rate type M for 27.07.2026 in the system settings'
Missing rate para esa combo + rate type + fecha.

Solución: OB08 → add row.

### 'Exchange rate difference: too big'
SAP compara rate del doc con TCURR — si difiere > tolerance → warning/error.

Tolerance en `OB64` (per company code).

## Foreign currency revaluation
Mes-end job `F.05` valuates open items en foreign currency using current TCURR rate.

Si FX cambió → gain/loss postea a P&L.

## Autorización
- `S_TABU_DIS` con auth group para TCURR
- `S_TCODE = OB08`

title: SAP OMR6: tolerance limits for invoice verification
tags: sap, omr6, tolerance, mm, invoice, mrbr
excerpt: Configurar límites de tolerancia para MIRO.
body:
## Uso
`OMR6` → tabla de tolerance keys por company code.

## Tolerance keys
- **AN** — small amount
- **BD** — cash discount amount check
- **BR** — % of variance from moving avg price
- **BW** — variance % from moving avg (blocked stock)
- **DQ** — quantity variance (excessive)
- **DW** — quantity variance (missing)
- **KW** — variance value (from PO)
- **LA** — amount of blanket PO
- **LD** — blanket PO time limit
- **PP** — price variance (% or absolute)
- **PS** — price variance (item, estimated)
- **ST** — date variance (order-based invoice)
- **VP** — moving avg price variance

## Configurar
Select company code → tolerance key → **Details**:
- **Do not check** (skip esta validación)
- **Absolute lower limit** + Percentage limit
- **Absolute upper limit** + Percentage limit

### Ejemplo PP (price variance)
```
Lower absolute: 100 EUR    ⏫
Upper absolute: 100 EUR
Lower percentage: 5%
Upper percentage: 5%
```

Significa: invoice price puede diferir del PO price hasta 5% o 100 EUR — el menor de los dos.

## Efecto en MIRO
### Dentro de tolerance
SAP acepta invoice sin block.

### Fuera de tolerance
- Warning message (user puede continuar) — depending on config
- Or blocked (payment block auto) — user posts pero factura no se paga hasta release

## Ver invoices blocked
`MRBR` — release blocked invoices:
- Filter por reason
- Muestra invoices con block

### Release
MRBR → select invoice → **Release** → ahora payable.

### Reason blocked
Invoice → **Block reason** column:
- **P** — price
- **Q** — quantity
- **A** — automatic block for GR-based IV
- Etc.

## Tolerance groups (advanced)
High-value users (buyers senior) pueden tener tolerance más amplia.

`OMR6` extends per tolerance group + user assignment en tolerance group config.

## Best practice
- **DQ** (quantity excess): tight — 0 tolerance in PRD normally
- **PP** (price): moderate — 3-5%
- **AN** (small amounts): amounts <5 EUR → auto-post sin verificar

## Ver settings actuales
```
SE16N → T169G — tolerance limits config
```

## Impacto downstream
- FBL1N shows blocked invoices con status
- F110 (payment run) skip blocked invoices
- Auditores revisan invoices blocked > X días como flag

## Autorización
- `M_RECH_BUK` — invoice verification
- `M_RECH_SPG` — release blocked (MRBR)

## Alternate: automatic release job
`MRBR` puede correr automáticamente en background:
- `SM36` → schedule `RM08RELEASE` diario
- Auto-release invoices blocked older than N días si nadie action manual

Useful en operaciones grandes.

title: SAP SPRO / IMG: customizing central
tags: sap, spro, img, customizing, config
excerpt: Implementation Guide — punto central de configuración SAP.
body:
## Uso
`SPRO` → botón **SAP Reference IMG** → árbol jerárquico de config por área funcional.

### Estructura típica
- **SAP NetWeaver** — cross-module
- **Cross-Application Components**
- **Enterprise Structure**
- **Financial Accounting**
- **Materials Management**
- **Sales and Distribution**
- **Controlling**
- **Human Resources**
- **Logistics — General**
- **Production Planning**
- **Quality Management**

## Uso típico
1. `SPRO` → **SAP Reference IMG**
2. Expandir el nodo relevant (ej: **Financial Accounting**)
3. Doble clic → puede abrir:
   - Tabla config (para editar directo)
   - Wizard / Guide
   - Otra transacción específica

## Ejemplos populares

### Company code setup
SPRO → Enterprise Structure → Definition → Financial Accounting → **Define Company Code**.

Or directo: `OX02`.

### Document number ranges
SPRO → FI → Document → **Number ranges → Documents**.
Or directo: `FBN1`.

### FI posting periods
SPRO → FI → Document → **Posting Periods → Open and Close Posting Periods**.
Or directo: `OB52`.

### Automatic account determination (SD)
SPRO → Sales → Basic Functions → **Account Assignment/Costing → Revenue Account Determination**.
Or directo: `VKOA`.

## Personalizar el IMG (project IMG)
`SPRO` → **Project Management**:
- Create project (implementation, upgrade, roll-out)
- Filter IMG a solo los nodos relevantes al proyecto
- Add-ons / country versions

## Verified transactions
Cada nodo IMG apunta a una transaction específica. Menú **Info** button en el nodo → ver.

## Transportar config
Al guardar cambios en IMG:
- SAP pide **customizing request** (workbench request no, customizing sí)
- Assign to existing o crear nuevo
- Al transportar → viaja customizing entre systems

## SCC4 setting
Algunos clients tienen 'Automatic recording of changes' — cada save prompts transport.
Otros 'No changes allowed' — cerrado en PRD.

## SPRO_ADMIN
Alternate tcode para administración de projects IMG.

## Search en IMG
**Ctrl+F** en el árbol → search por keyword.

O **SPRO_SEARCH** para búsqueda avanzada.

## Documentation
Cada nodo IMG tiene **Documentation** button — SAP-standard help para esa config.

## Autorización
- `S_PROJECT` — project management
- `S_IMG_ACTV` — IMG activity
- + auth de la tabla config subyacente (`S_TABU_DIS`)

## Modificar customizing masivo
- Change vía SE16N (SAP standard tables) → **NO recomendado**
- Usar siempre el IMG path official — SAP valida consistency

## Comparar entre systems
`SCU0` — customizing comparison:
- Sistema origen vs destino
- Muestra rows different
- Cross-check post-transport

## Post-upgrade
`SPDD/SPAU` para adjust modifications.
`SPRO_ADMIN` → create upgrade project.

title: SAP F110: payment run automático
tags: sap, f110, payment, run, ap, vendor
excerpt: Correr proceso automatizado de pagos a proveedores.
body:
## Uso
`F110` → payment run.

### Header
- **Run date** (fecha del run)
- **Identification** (ID único para el run, ej: `PAY001`)

## Steps del payment run

### 1. Parameters (tab)
- **Posting date** (fecha contable)
- **Docs entered up to** (fecha corte)
- **Customer/vendor items due by** (due date)
- **Company codes**: seleccionar
- **Payment methods**: E = electronic transfer, C = check, T = tape (SEPA)
- **Next payment run**

### 2. Free selection (tab)
Opcional: filtros adicionales:
- Vendor account
- Doc type
- Assignment

### 3. Proposal
**Schedule Proposal** button:
- SAP identifica invoices due to pay
- Genera propuesta (test mode)

### 4. Ver propuesta
**Edit Proposal** button:
- Ver items seleccionados
- **Change payment block**: excluir/incluir manualmente
- **Change house bank** o **payment method** individual
- Save propuesta

### 5. Payment run
**Schedule Payment Run** button:
- Executes real posting
- Genera clearing docs + payment docs

### 6. Print media / DME
**Schedule Print Program** button:
- Print checks
- Generar DME (Data Medium Exchange) file para transfer al banco
- Format: SEPA XML, ACH, etc.

## Ver payment log
Después de each step:
- **Additional log**: log summary
- **Proposal log**: what was selected/why

## Errores comunes

### 'No documents selected for payment'
- Filter demasiado restrictivo
- No hay items due (fechas)
- Vendor blocked for payment (`XK02` → block for payment)

### 'Cannot determine payment method'
- Vendor sin payment method en tab **Payment** (XK02)
- Payment method del PO/factura mismatch

### 'House bank determination failed'
- Custom → house bank en XK02 vendor master
- Or config table for automatic determination based on currency/amount/etc.

### 'Excluded from payment: exception'
- Individual invoice tiene payment block (R = invoice verification, X = other)
- Release en MRBR o FBL1N

## Test mode vs live
- **Test run**: no postings, solo report
- **Live run**: postea real

Siempre test primero, review proposal, then live.

## Recurring monthly / weekly
`F110` puede ser scheduled en background:
- `SM36` → job type = program `SAPF110V`
- Or F110 → **Program** → **Schedule Payment Run** with variant

## Ver history de runs
`F110` → menu **Environment** → **Payment history** → previous runs con stats.

## Cancel un run
Si hubo error después de post pero antes de print media:
- `F110` → **Environment** → **Cancel Payment Documents** (F.13)

CUIDADO — reverse de payment run es complicado, reversa cada payment doc individually.

## DME file — enviar al banco
After print program:
- File location: `/usr/sap/<SID>/DVEBMGS<inst>/data/` (o custom path)
- Download to local
- Upload via banking portal (SFTP)
- O direct integration (SAP Cash Management)

## SEPA / ISO 20022
European payment format estándar.

Config en `FBZP` → payment method → **DMEE** — tree structure define XML output.

## Autorización
- `F_REGU_BUK` — payment program per company code
- `F_REGU_KOA` — account type
- `F_KOSP_BUK` — payment terms

title: SAP AS03/AS02/AS01: asset master (Fixed Assets)
tags: sap, as01, as02, as03, asset, fixed asset, faa
excerpt: Gestión de master de activos fijos.
body:
## Transacciones
- `AS01` — create
- `AS02` — change
- `AS03` — display

## Uso AS03
Asset number + subnumber + company code → Enter.

SAP number format: XXXXXXXXXXXX-YYYY (main-sub).

## Tabs (AS03)
### General
- Description
- Serial number
- Inventory number
- Manufacturer
- Cost center (responsable)
- Plant / location

### Time-dependent
- Cost center (per period)
- Plant
- Person responsible
- Business area

### Allocations
- Investment order (KO) — si viene de investment
- WBS element — si viene de project

### Origin
- Vendor
- PO reference
- Original acquisition date
- Country of origin
- Original asset (if partial transfer)

### Net Worth Tax
Relevant para tax reporting específico.

### Insurance
- Insurance company
- Value insured

### Leasing
Si es leased asset, terms.

### Depreciation Areas (tabs por area)
- **01** — Book depreciation (local GAAP)
- **15** — Tax depreciation
- **30** — Group (IFRS)
- Etc.

Cada area con:
- Useful life
- Depreciation key
- Start date

## Ver valores actuales
`AW01N` — Asset Explorer:
- Acquisition value
- Accumulated depreciation
- Net book value
- Depreciation por período (planned + posted)

## Posting valores al asset

### Acquisition
- **F-90** — post directly to asset
- Or from **MIRO** (invoice with account assignment 'A' = asset)

### Retirement (venta / scrap)
- **F-92** — retirement with revenue (venta)
- **F-91** — retirement without revenue (scrap)

### Transfer
- **ABUMN** — transfer entre asset numbers

### Depreciation
- Auto-calculated por SAP
- Run mensual: `AFAB` — depreciation posting run

## Depreciation keys (config)
`AFAMA` — depreciation key definition.

Common:
- **LINR** — linear (straight-line)
- **DEG** — declining balance
- **DEG2** — double declining
- **MANU** — manual (calculate outside)

Assigned per depreciation area en asset master.

## Depreciation run (`AFAB`)
Mensual:

title: SAP MB1B/MB1A/MB1C: goods movements clásicos
tags: sap, mb1a, mb1b, mb1c, transfer, gi, mm
excerpt: Transacciones legacy para movimientos, alternative a MIGO.
body:
## Uso
- `MB1A` — goods issue (movement type 201, 261, 281, etc.)
- `MB1B` — transfer posting (301, 311, 321, etc.)
- `MB1C` — other goods receipt (501, 561)

## MIGO vs MB1*
- **MIGO**: transaction moderna, más versátil (single UI para todo)
- **MB1A/B/C**: legacy pero más rápido/simple

Ambos generan mismos material documents (misma tabla `MSEG`).

## MB1B: transfer entre plants
### Ejemplo
Transferir 100 units material X del plant 1000 → plant 2000.

1. `MB1B`
2. **Movement type**: `301` (transfer plant to plant, one step)
3. **Plant**: 1000 (source)
4. **Storage location**: `S001` (source)
5. Enter

6. **Material**: X
7. **Quantity**: 100
8. **Receiving plant**: 2000
9. **Receiving sloc**: S010
10. Save (Ctrl+S)

### Two-step transfer (313 + 315)
Si es transfer lento entre plants distintas:
- **313** — remove from source plant (in-transit)
- **315** — receive at destination

Se emite el 313 al despachar, y 315 al recibir físicamente. En medio, stock aparece 'in-transit' (visible en MMBE).

## MB1A: goods issue

### 201 — GI a cost center
1. `MB1A`
2. Movement type: `201`
3. Plant + SLoc source

4. Material + Quantity
5. **Cost center** (dónde cargar el gasto)
6. Save

### 261 — GI a production order
1. `MB1A` → mvt `261`
2. Reference: **Order** field → PP order number
3. SAP trae componentes del BOM
4. Confirm qty
5. Save

### 281 — GI a project (WBS)
1. `MB1A` → mvt `281`
2. WBS element

## MB1C: other GR

### 501 — GR sin PO
Entry de material without PO reference (samples, corrections):
1. `MB1C` → mvt `501`
2. Plant + SLoc
3. Material + quantity
4. **G/L account** (offsetting account, e.g., expense)
5. Save

### 561 — initial stock upload
Cargar stock inicial al implementar sistema:
1. `MB1C` → mvt `561`
2. Value = current book value (para valuation)

**Cuidado**: 561 movements van a un GL account específico (usually 'inventory offsetting' — configured in OMWN).

## Reason for movement
Algunos movement types require razón:
- 551 (scrap) — reason: broken, expired, damage
- 122 (return to vendor) — reason: quality issue, wrong item

Configurable en `OMBS`.

## Batch and serial numbers
Si material batch-managed:
- Batch field required (or auto-determinated)
- MB1B con 311 → both plants must have batch mgmt config compatible

## Print label / print form
At save:
- Message determination (config en `NACE`) may trigger label print
- Output types: `NEU` (new)

## Errores comunes

### 'Deficit of ... stock'
GI de más stock del disponible:
- Ver stock actual: `MMBE`
- Solicitar transfer to source first
- O ajustar quantity

### 'Batch does not exist'
Material con batch mgmt pero batch not created:
- Auto-creation on GR según config
- Or manual: `MSC1N`

### 'Plant not authorized for movement type'
Auth object `M_MSEG_BWA` no permite ese mvt type + plant.

## Reverse
Movements pueden cancelarse:
- `MBST` o via `MIGO` action=Cancellation → reference the material doc

## Ver history
`MB51` — material document list.

## Autorización
- `M_MSEG_BMB` — general
- `M_MSEG_BWA` — movement type
- `M_MSEG_WMB` — plant

## MIGO — equivalent moderno
MB1B `301` = MIGO Action=Transfer, Reference=Other, Mvt=301.

Users prefieren MB1* por ser rápido con hotkeys.

title: SAP OB52: open/close FI posting periods
tags: sap, ob52, posting period, fi, close, open
excerpt: Abrir/cerrar períodos contables para postings.
body:
## Uso
`OB52` → tabla `T001B` (posting period variants).

### Estructura
Cada company code se asigna a una posting period variant. Multiple company codes pueden compartir variant.

## Ver actual
`OB52` → **Change** o **Display**:

- **Variant**: identifier (ej: `0001`)
- **A (Account Type)**:
  - `+` — all accounts (default)
  - `A` — asset
  - `D` — customer (AR)
  - `K` — vendor (AP)
  - `M` — material
  - `S` — GL
- **From account** / **To account**: rango
- **From period 1** / **To period 1**: primer bucket abierto (usually current)
- **Year**: fiscal year
- **From period 2** / **To period 2**: segundo bucket (usually 12+special periods para year-end)
- **Auth group**: quién puede postear (adicional)

## Ejemplo config típico
```
0001  +   (blank)  (blank)  6  2026  7  2026
```
Significa: para variant 0001, todos los accounts (+), períodos 6-7 de 2026 open.

## Cerrar período
1. OB52 → Change
2. Editar la row → cambiar 'From period 1' de 6 → 7
3. Save (transport request)

Ahora período 6 está cerrado, solo se puede postear en 7+.

## Ejemplo real: cierre de mes
Es 5 de agosto. Cerrar período 7 (julio):
1. Antes: `6 2026  8 2026` (junio y julio abiertos + agosto)
2. Después de cerrar: `7 2026  8 2026` (solo julio y agosto)
3. Después de finalizar cierre: `8 2026  8 2026` (solo agosto)

## Special periods
Períodos 13-16 = 'special periods' (adjustments year-end):
- No corresponden a mes calendario
- Usados para closing entries (accruals, adjustments)
- Config en period 2 range: `From 13, To 16`

## Ver quién intentó postear en período cerrado
`SM21` — system log con mensaje 'Posting period X not open'.

## Autorization group
Column 'Auth. Group' en OB52:
- Define un tag → users con auth object `F_BKPF_BLA` con el mismo tag pueden postear
- Common use: 'CLOSE' tag → solo Finance team puede postear en período recién cerrado (adjustments)

## User exit para excepciones
SAP ofrece BAdI para bypass en casos específicos (raro, no recomendado).

## Ver postings hacía un período
`FS10N` con año fiscal / period range → ver actividad.

## Errors comunes

### 'Posting period XX not open in company code YYYY'
- OB52 verificar variant asignada al CC (transacción `OBBP`)
- Abrir período temporalmente si legítima excepción

### 'Period is closed for account type X'
OB52 tiene múltiples rows por A (account type). Puede tener GL abierto pero AR cerrado.

### 'System locked'
While OB52 en modo change → otros users no pueden postear. Save + confirm.

## Cross-module periods
Otras transacciones relacionadas:
- **MMPV / MMRV** — MM period open (goods movements)
- **AJRW** — FI-AA fiscal year change (assets)
- **AJAB** — FI-AA year-end close

Estas son separadas de OB52 (FI). Cerrar todos coordinadamente.

## Autorización
- `S_TABU_DIS` con auth group para `T001B`
- `S_TCODE = OB52`
- Restringido típicamente a admin Finance

title: SAP MMPV / MMRV: open/close MM periods
tags: sap, mmpv, mmrv, mm, period, close
excerpt: Cerrar período MM (goods movements) al fin de mes.
body:
## Contexto
MM tiene su propio period control separado de FI (OB52).

MM period define en qué mes se pueden postear goods movements (MIGO, MB1*).

## MMRV: view current period
`MMRV` → company code → **Enter**:
- **Current period**: mes fiscal actual
- **Previous period**: mes anterior (aún abierto para adjustments)

## MMPV: change period
Run al fin de mes para 'roll forward':
1. `MMPV` → variant o direct
2. **Company codes**: seleccionar
3. **Period**: nuevo current period (ej: 8 para agosto)
4. **Fiscal year**: 2026
5. **Check and close period**: yes (default)

Execute → SAP:
1. Cierra período viejo (7, julio)
2. Abre período nuevo (8, agosto)
3. Anterior period (7) queda como 'previous period' — aún permite algunos postings limited

## Restricciones
- Solo puede rolar 1 período por vez
- No skip: no ir de 7 directo a 9 sin pasar por 8

## Backdate posting
Con MM ROLL FORWARD hecho:
- Postings del mes cerrado (July) fail
- Except si:
  - Marca 'Allow posting to previous period' en config (`OMSY`)
  - Doc type específico permite (`OMKG`)

## Reset periodo (backwards) — casi nunca
MMPV solo roll forward. Para 'volver' a periodo anterior:
- Contactar SAP support
- Alternate: usar special periods FI (13-16)

## Consequences de cerrar sin querer
Si cerraste period 7 pero necesitás postear más al 7:
- OMSY → cambiar setting 'previous period allowed' temporarily
- Post document (mvt type)
- Return setting al default

## Ver logs de MMPV
`SLG1` con object `MM_MMPV`.

O log del job en SM37.

## Programar MMPV mensual
`SM36` → schedule `RMMMPERI` (program de MMPV) para día 1 de cada mes.

### Variant
Set variant con:
- Company codes
- Period selection: **Increment period by 1**

## Errores comunes

### 'Postings still exist for period X'
MMPV chequea que no haya movements pendientes en el period vieja. Si hay backlog:
- Force close (checkbox)
- Or fix backlog first

### 'Fiscal year change required'
At turn of year:
- MMPV va de period 12 to period 1 of next year
- Requires assets fiscal year change first (`AJRW`)

## OMSY — MM period config
- **Allow posting to previous period**: yes/no per period type
- **Backup for backward postings**: yes/no

Configurar cauteloso.

## Coordinación con FI
Orden típico end-month:
1. MM: cerrar period con MMPV
2. FI: correr `F.05` (foreign currency revaluation) — puede requerir open MM
3. FI: adjustments
4. FI: cerrar period con OB52
5. CO / Assets closing steps

## Autorización
- `M_MRV_BUK` — MM period per company code
- `M_MMPV_BUK` — MMPV execution

title: SAP F.05: foreign currency revaluation
tags: sap, f.05, revaluation, foreign currency, fi
excerpt: Revalorar posiciones abiertas en moneda extranjera al cierre.
body:
## Contexto
Invoices en foreign currency (USD, EUR) postean con exchange rate del día del posting.

Al cierre de mes, se recalcula el value en local currency (COP, MXN) usando FX rate actual → gain/loss.

## Uso
`F.05` → selection:
- **Company code**
- **Evaluation key date** (usually last day of month)
- **Valuation method**: config methode (ver next)
- **Reset**: si es reverse post (default en next period)
- **Ledger** (multi-ledger environments)

## Valuation methods
Config `OB59`:
- **BADEBIT**: post to bank account
- **VALLOCK**: exact
- **P&L account** for gain/loss

Métodos comunes:
- **BUCH** — book (revaluation to leading ledger only)
- **PARA1/PARA2** — parallel ledgers

## Ejecutar
1. F.05 → parametros
2. **Test run** — check preview sin postear
3. Ver **Report list** — items evaluados + gain/loss por item
4. **Live run** — post GL entries

## Postings generados

### Vendor con invoice USD (positive balance)
- Original: 1000 USD @ rate 4000 = 4,000,000 COP
- At period end: rate 4200
- Nueva valuation: 4,200,000 COP → diff +200,000 COP = FX gain

Posting:
- Debit vendor recon account (unrealized loss FX)
- Credit FX Gain P&L account

### Customer con invoice USD (positive receivable)
- Similar concept but reversed sign

## Reset (importante!)
Default: revaluation is 'reset' at start of next period.

Si rate revierte, la revaluation posting también.

Sin reset → double count.

## Ver postings generados
- Doc type especial (SC, SB) — configurable
- FBL1N/FBL5N muestra revaluation postings con flag

## Currency types
For multi-currency systems:
- Local (10) — company code currency
- Group (30) — corporate currency
- Hard (40) — inflation-resistant

Cada currency type revaluated separately.

## Common issues

### 'No exchange rate maintained'
Missing row en TCURR (`OB08`) para date/currency/rate type.

Fix: OB08 → add row.

### 'Balance sheet valuation area not configured'
OB59 → verify method config + accounts.

### 'Revaluation adjustment > tolerance'
Tolerance limits per company code en config.

## Best practice
- Correr F.05 en fin de mes en test
- Review differences con business
- Live run
- Verify GL balances after
- Reset in next period (auto)

## Related
- **FAGL_FC_VALUATION** — S/4HANA equivalent (new GL)
- **F-51** — batch: revalue open items
- **FSCU** — currency translation post-valuation

## Autorización
- `F_BKPF_BUK` — company code
- `F_BKPF_BLA` — doc type SC
- `F_FBSK_VAL` — valuation type

title: SAP RSA1: BW admin — process chains
tags: sap, rsa1, bw, data warehouse, process chain, dtp
excerpt: Administración de SAP BW / BW4HANA — process chains y data flow.
body:
## Contexto
SAP BW (Business Warehouse) es data warehouse SAP. Carga datos de SAP ECC / S/4 + externals a un modelo dimensional para reporting.

`RSA1` = Data Warehouse Workbench.

## Menú principal
### Modeling
- **InfoAreas** — organizar objects
- **InfoObjects** — dimensions/keyfigures
- **InfoProviders** — DSO, cube, MultiProvider, HANA calc view
- **InfoSources** — data extractors
- **Data Sources** — origin data
- **Transformations** — mapping source → target

### Administration
- **Process Chains**
- **Monitor** — data loads status
- **Metadata Repository**

## Data flow típico
```
Source (ECC) → DataSource → PSA (Persistent Staging Area)
                                ↓ Transformation
                            DSO (advanced or classic)
                                ↓
                            InfoCube / HANA view
                                ↓
                            Query / dashboard
```

## Process chain
Sequencia orquestada de tareas de carga:
- Start process (schedule / manual / event)
- Load DataSource
- Activate DSO
- Load InfoCube
- Delete PSA / index
- Compress cube
- Send notification email

## Crear process chain
`RSPC` — process chain maintenance:
1. Create → nombre + description
2. Drag processes desde catálogo
3. Connect con arrows (dependencies)
4. Assign variants (settings específicos)
5. Activate

## Ver chain status
`RSPC` → chain → Log:
- **Green** — success
- **Yellow** — running
- **Red** — failed

### Failed step
Right-click en el step failed → **Display log** → error message.

### Continue after fix
- **Repeat** — retry step
- **Force in green** — mark ok manually (bypass — cuidadoso!)

## Load monitoring
`RSMO` — general monitor for load requests:
- Ver requests activos + completed
- Filter por status
- Drill down a details

## Delta loads
DataSources delta:
- Init con full load
- Then delta captures cambios (via delta pointer o CDC)
- Enable delta: `RSA7` (source system) — delta queue

## Full vs delta
- **Full** — todo cada vez (small tables)
- **Delta** — solo cambios (large tables, transaction data)

Configurable en DataSource + DTP (Data Transfer Process).

## Cubes and DSOs

### Classic DSO
- **Standard DSO** — 3 tables (activation queue, active data, change log)
- Merge duplicates by key

### Cube
- Multi-dimensional model
- Fact table + dimensions
- Read-optimized (writes are aggregates)

### HANA calc view (BW4HANA)
- In-memory modeling
- No physical storage → live query at runtime

## Common tasks

### Delete un load fallido
`RSMO` → seleccionar request → **Delete** → confirms.

Data con estado 'red' se puede eliminar. 'Green' request en DSO ya activated → más complejo.

### Rollback DSO activation
RSA1 → DSO → **Manage** → **Reconstruction/Rollback**.

Revierte a state anterior.

### Optimize cube performance
- Compress: elimina duplicates y agrupa
- Aggregates: pre-calc common groupings
- Partitioning: cube in months/quarters

## RSA3 — extractor checker
Simulate el extract del source system (source-side sanity check).

## RSPC transporting
Process chains + objects transportables. Cambios en DEV → transport → QA → PRD.

## Autorización
- `S_RS_ADSO` — advanced DSO
- `S_RS_ISOUR` — data source
- `S_RS_RSTT` — testing
- `S_RS_PC` — process chain

## S/4 HANA embedded analytics
S/4HANA tiene analytics en-CDS-view built-in, reduciendo necesidad de BW en algunos casos. BW sigue vigente para escenarios enterprise complex.

title: SAP: variantes de reports (SE38 variant)
tags: sap, variant, se38, report, save, protection
excerpt: Guardar y reutilizar variantes para reports pesados.
body:
## Contexto
Ejecutar el mismo report con mismos parámetros repetidamente → save variant → 1 click reuse.

## Crear variant
1. `SE38` → programa (ej: `RFITEMAP` — vendor line items)
2. Execute (F8) → selection screen aparece
3. Fill parameters (dates, company code, filters)
4. Menu **Goto** → **Variants** → **Save as Variant**
5. Attributes:
   - **Variant name**: `Z_MENSUAL_AP`
   - **Meaning**: 'Reporte AP mensual'
   - **Only for background processing**: yes/no
   - **Protect variant**: yes = solo owner puede modificar
   - **Environment-specific**: development/test/production

6. Save

## Ejecutar con variant
1. `SE38` → programa → **Execute**
2. Menu **Get variant** (F17)
3. Seleccionar variant
4. **Parametros load automatically** → F8

## Attributes advanced

### Selection variables
Para fechas dinámicas — 'end of month', 'last week':
1. Al save variant → tab **Attributes** para cada field
2. **Selection variable type**:
   - **D** — Dynamic date calculation (e.g., 'End of previous month')
   - **B** — Table (get from table lookup)

### Attribute values
- 'End of previous month': type D, name `M-1L`
- 'Start of current year': type D, name `AT`
- 'Yesterday': type D, name `T-1`

List en SAP note oficial.

## Field attributes
En variant maintenance, cada field puede tener:
- **Protected** — user no puede cambiar (locked)
- **Hidden** — no aparece en selection screen
- **Only for background**: solo visible en batch
- **GPA off** — no user parameters

Use case: variant estándar para users, con fields protected para prevenir cambios.

## Delete variant
SE38 → programa → **Variants** → **Delete** → seleccionar variant.

## Copy variant
`Utilities` → **Copy variant** → nueva.

## Variant maintenance transaction
`SC38` — direct variant editor.

O desde SE38 → button 'Variant maintenance'.

## Transportar variant
Variants entre systems (DEV → QA → PRD):
- Al save variant → SAP puede pedir transport request (marcar 'System-wide')
- Or manual: `SE38` → **Variants** → **Utilities** → **Transport variants**

## Ver quién usó un variant
`SE38` → Variants → seleccionar → **Attributes** → **Environment info**.

## Standard variants shipped
SAP a veces incluye variants standard (`SAP_`) — no modificar directly, copy first.

## Multi-language
Descriptions traducibles:
- Variant → **Attributes** → **Description** → multi-language via **Translate** button

## Batch execution
Job variants scheduled en `SM36`:
- Program: `RFITEMAP`
- Variant: `Z_MENSUAL_AP`
- Recurring monthly

Ejecuta variant identico cada mes.

## Common issues

### 'Variant does not exist'
Deleted or transport failed.

Recrear o restore from history.

### 'Variant contains invalid values'
Field cambió de type (dev change) but variant guarda old format.

Solución: re-save variant.

### Values sensitive stored
Variant puede contener passwords/PII — cuidado, especialmente si transportado.

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` para crear variants shared
- Users pueden crear propios variants (`U`) sin dev auth
- `S_TRANSPRT` para transport

## Alternativa: SUBMIT com variant en ABAP
```abap
SUBMIT rfitemap
  USING SELECTION-SET 'Z_MENSUAL_AP'
  AND RETURN.
```

Call variant de otro programa.

title: SAP: SBWP notifications programáticas
tags: sap, sbwp, notification, workflow, email, bapi
excerpt: Enviar notificaciones al Business Workplace desde ABAP.
body:
## Uso
Desde ABAP, function modules para enviar docs al inbox de otro user:

### SO_DOCUMENT_SEND_API1 (basic)
```abap
DATA: ls_docdata TYPE sodocchgi1,
      lt_body TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF solisti1,
      lt_receivers TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF somlreci1,
      ls_receiver TYPE somlreci1,
      ls_line TYPE solisti1.

ls_docdata-obj_name = 'ZALERT'.
ls_docdata-obj_descr = 'Ticket urgente: acción requerida'.
ls_docdata-doc_size = 500.

ls_line-line = 'Hola,'.
APPEND ls_line TO lt_body.
ls_line-line = ''.
APPEND ls_line TO lt_body.
ls_line-line = 'Se detectó un problema en el proceso XYZ.'.
APPEND ls_line TO lt_body.

ls_receiver-receiver = 'JPEREZ'.
ls_receiver-rec_type = 'B'.   " B = SAP username
ls_receiver-express = 'X'.    " popup instant
APPEND ls_receiver TO lt_receivers.

CALL FUNCTION 'SO_DOCUMENT_SEND_API1'
  EXPORTING
    document_data              = ls_docdata
    document_type              = 'RAW'
    put_in_outbox              = 'X'
    commit_work                = 'X'
  TABLES
    object_content             = lt_body
    receivers                  = lt_receivers
  EXCEPTIONS
    too_many_receivers         = 1
    document_not_sent          = 2
    OTHERS                     = 8.
```

### Receiver types
- **B** — SAP user (username)
- **U** — Internet email
- **X** — X400 address
- **F** — Fax
- **G** — Distribution list

## Con attachment
```abap
DATA: lt_attach TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF solisti1,
      lt_pack TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sopcklsti1.

" Attach PDF
DATA(lv_pdf_binary) = ... " get PDF binary somehow

DATA(ls_pack) = VALUE sopcklsti1( 
    transf_bin = 'X'
    head_start = 1
    head_num = 0
    body_start = 1
    body_num = <size_in_lines>
    doc_type = 'PDF'
    obj_descr = 'reporte.pdf'
    obj_name = 'REPORTE'
    doc_size = <size_bytes>
).
APPEND ls_pack TO lt_pack.

" Add binary content to lt_attach

CALL FUNCTION 'SO_DOCUMENT_SEND_API1'
  EXPORTING ...
  TABLES
    packing_list = lt_pack
    contents_hex = lt_attach   " binary
    contents_txt = lt_body     " body text
    receivers = lt_receivers.
```

## Send to internet email (outside SAP)
Receiver type 'U' + address:
```abap
ls_receiver-receiver = 'jperez@empresa.com'.
ls_receiver-rec_type = 'U'.
```

Requires SCOT SMTP configured.

## Send job to run RSCONN01
Email no sale automáticamente. Necesita el job:
- `SM36` schedule `RSCONN01` cada 5 min → dispatcher

## Ver enviados
`SBWP` → **Outbox** → tu propio outbox.
`SOST` — status monitor global.

## Modern API: BCS (Business Communication Services)
S/4HANA prefiere BCS classes:
```abap
DATA(lo_send) = cl_bcs=>create_persistent( ).

DATA(lo_doc) = cl_document_bcs=>create_document(
  i_type    = 'RAW'
  i_text    = lt_body
  i_subject = 'Ticket urgente'
).
lo_send->set_document( lo_doc ).

DATA(lo_recv) = cl_cam_address_bcs=>create_internet_address(
  i_address_string = 'jperez@empresa.com'
).
lo_send->add_recipient( lo_recv ).

lo_send->send( i_with_error_screen = abap_true ).
COMMIT WORK.
```

Más OO, más flexible.

## Common issues

### Email 'stuck' en outbox
- SCOT dispatcher job (RSCONN01) not running
- SMTP server unreachable
- SBWP → Outbox → status del item

### Wrong sender
Default sender = user's email (from SU01) or default domain.
Override via `sender_of_document` in `SO_DOCUMENT_SEND_API1`.

### 'Address not defined'
Receiver username no válido en SAP. Verify SU01.

## Templates
Standard SAP office templates: `SO10`.

Más sofisticado — SmartForms / Adobe Forms para HTML/PDF-rich content.

## Autorización
- `S_OC_SEND` — send documents
- `S_OC_DOC` — create documents
- `S_ADMI_FCD = SOSN` — SOST admin

title: SAP: rate limiting y throttling en SAP Gateway (OData)
tags: sap, gateway, odata, throttling, rate limit, fiori
excerpt: Protecciones para OData services expuestos externamente.
body:
## SAP Gateway components
- **Hub deployment**: Gateway server separado del backend ECC/S4
- **Embedded deployment**: Gateway como service dentro del backend (S/4HANA moderno)

## Ver OData services registrados
`/IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE` — main maintenance.

Lista de services + status:
- **Registered**
- **Active**

Registrar new: **Add Service** → seleccionar del backend catalog.

## Test service
`/IWFND/GW_CLIENT` — Gateway client:
- URL: `/sap/opu/odata/sap/<service_name>/`
- Method: GET / POST
- Headers: Authorization, ContentType
- Body: JSON o XML

SAP client integrated — no browser required.

## Ver logs de calls
`/IWFND/APPS_LOG` — application log.
`/IWFND/ERROR_LOG` — errors por service.
`/IWFND/TRACES` — HTTP trace per call.

## Performance
`/IWFND/STATS` — statistics por service:
- Total calls
- Avg response time
- Errors count

## Cache
OData services pueden cachear responses.

### Configurar cache
Service → **Metadata Cache** — TTL config.

Reset cache:
`/IWBEP/CACHE_CLEANUP` or `/IWFND/CACHE_CLEANUP`

## Session management
### Stateless (recomendado)
Cada request es independiente — no session persistente.

Más escalable, sin state en el server.

### Stateful
Para long-running scenarios (rare in OData).

## Auth
### Basic auth
User + password en HTTP Basic (base64). Malo para producción.

### SAML SSO
 Standard corporate — token issued by IdP.

### OAuth 2.0
Recomendado para public APIs.
- **Client credentials** — server-to-server
- **Auth code** — user-facing

Config en `/IWFND/OAUTH_ADMIN`.

### Certificate (X.509)
Client cert-based auth for high-security scenarios.

## Throttling
### Native SAP
Gateway 8.0+ tiene rate limiting built-in:
- Configurar en profile parameter `iwbeprules/*`
- Or ICF service throttling (`SICF`)

### Reverse proxy layer
Más común: SAP Web Dispatcher / NetWeaver Gateway hub con rate limit externo:
- Nginx / F5 / Cloudflare enfrente
- Rate limit by IP, by user, by client_id

## Common issues

### 'HTTP 429 Too Many Requests'
Rate limit hit. Backoff + retry after `Retry-After` header.

### 'Session expired'
Long-idle session, need to re-authenticate.

### 'CSRF token required'
SAP Gateway requires CSRF token for POST/PUT/DELETE:
1. First: GET request con header `X-CSRF-Token: Fetch`
2. Server responde con token in header
3. POST includes token in `X-CSRF-Token: <value>`

### 'Metadata timeout'
Metadata muy grande → GET metadata tarda:
- Deep filter `$select` para reduce
- Server-side pagination `$top` `$skip`

## Best practices
- Small responses (`$select`, `$expand` sparingly)
- Pagination for lists (`$top=50`, `$skiptoken=xxx`)
- Batch requests (`$batch` endpoint)
- Client caching (Etag / If-None-Match)

## Autorización
- `S_SERVICE` — service metadata
- `/IWFND/*` — Gateway framework
- + backend auth (business objects)

## Related transactions
- `/IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE` — service registry
- `/IWFND/EXT_SERVICES` — external services
- `/IWBEP/SERVICE_MAINT` — service in backend
- `/N/IWBEP/REG_SERVICE` — register new

## Idiomas soportados
Cada SAP system multi-lingual. Idiomas instalados visibles en `SMLT`:
- **E** — English
- **S** — Spanish
- **D** — German
- **F** — French

- Etc.

Install languages via SMLT o Import Packages.

## Ver / editar traducciones
`SE63` — Translation Environment.

### Types
- **ABAP Editor** — code comments/messages
- **Text elements** — text symbols del report
- **Data Elements** — labels de fields (short, medium, long, heading)
- **Domain values** — valid values (T/F, active/inactive)
- **GUI titles** — screen titles
- **Message classes** — messages de error/info

## Ejemplo: traducir data element
1. SE63 → **Translation** → **Data element (DE)**
2. Object name: `MATNR`
3. Source language: E (English)
4. Target language: S (Spanish)

### Ver texts actuales
- Short field label: `Mat. no.`
- Medium: `Material No.`
- Long: `Material Number`
- Heading: `Material`

### Traducción
- Short: `No. mat.`
- Medium: `No. Material`
- Long: `Número de Material`
- Heading: `Material`

Save.

## Bulk translation con `Se63 → Translation Object`
Multiple objects a la vez con filter.

## Package-level translation
`SE63` → **Translation** → **Package** → select package.

Muestra todos los objects del package pending translation.

Útil para roll-out de módulo/proyecto complete a nuevo idioma.

## Login default language
User → SU01 → tab **Defaults** → **Logon Language**:
- ES para spanish
- EN for english

User puede override at login screen.

## System default language
Profile parameter `zcsa/system_language`:
```
RZ11 → zcsa/system_language
```

## Report en language específico
Ejecutar `RFBILA00` en Spanish:
- Logon language: ES
- O ejecutar el program con language override

## Custom Z programs
When you create Z program:
- Texts (SE38 → **Text Elements**) in original language
- Translate a otros idiomas via SE63

Sin traducción, user en Spanish ve texts en English (fallback).

## Common issues

### 'Language not maintained'
- Text no traducido → SAP fallback a base language

### System doesn't have language installed
- SMLT → install language package first
- Import addon con language file

### Special characters
Use Unicode systems (Unicode kernel). Old MDMP setups don't handle Spanish accents well.

## SmartForms / Adobe Forms
Usan text modules — translation via `SE63 → Forms/Styles` category.

## Fiori translations
UI5 apps: translation en i18n files (properties files).

- Business Application Studio / VS Code — edit i18n files

title: SAP: monitoreo de RFC gateway (SMGW)
tags: sap, smgw, gateway, rfc, tcp, security
excerpt: Monitor y config del RFC gateway server.
body:
## Uso
`SMGW` — SAP Gateway Monitor.

### Dashboard
- **Connections** — active RFC connections
- **Threads** — server threads
- **Log** — recent gateway events

## Ver active connections
`SMGW` → **Goto → Connections**:
- Local
- Remote (external systems calling in)
- Program IDs registered

### Details per connection
- Client
- IP
- User
- Program ID
- Started time

## Log events
`SMGW` → **Goto → Logging**:
- Actions: log to file
- **Reg./Cancel of RFC servers**
- **Errors**

### Common events
- **Program ID XX registered** — RFC server available for calls
- **Registration/Deregistration** — client come/go
- **Access denied** — ACL blocked

## Registered program IDs
External RFC servers (e.g., PI/PO middleware, custom apps) register program IDs:
- SAP calls this ID via SM59 RFC destination type T (TCP/IP)
- Program executes RFC en el external system

### Ver registered
`SMGW → Goto → Displayed program IDs`.

## Security

### reginfo (registration info)
File en OS: `/usr/sap/<SID>/SYS/global/reginfo`

Controls WHICH program IDs can register:
```
# Example reginfo
P TP=SAPXPG HOST=* ACCESS=* CANCEL=*
P TP=my_ext_server HOST=external.local ACCESS=internal.local CANCEL=internal.local
```

Regex del TP, HOST, etc.

### secinfo (start info)
Controls WHO can start programs via CBS:
```
# secinfo
P TP=* USER=* HOST=* USER-HOST=*
```

### Reload after changes
`SMGW → Goto → Expert Functions → External Security → Reread`.

O restart gateway.

### Ver current reginfo
`SMGW → Goto → Expert Functions → External Security → reginfo`.

## Common security issues

### 'Program registration blocked'
reginfo doesn't allow this TP/HOST.

Solution: add entry a reginfo → reload.

### 'Externally executed program blocked'
secinfo blocks. Same fix.

### Unauthorized program registration attack
Malicious registration attempts logged:
```
SMGW → Log → filter for 'ACL' or 'denied'
```

Block IP en firewall external.

## Params importantes
```
gw/acl_mode = 1                # enforce reginfo/secinfo (default OK)
gw/reg_no_conn_info = 0        # log denials
gw/logging = ACTION=SPRZmt LOGFILE=gw_log-%y-%m-%d LFMT=%
```

RZ11 to view / modify.

## Restart gateway
Graceful:
```
SMGW → Goto → Expert Functions → Cancel gateway
```

Or OS command:
```
su - <sid>adm
sapcontrol -nr <inst> -function RestartService
```

## Ver stats
`SMGW → Goto → Statistics`:
- Total connections
- Peak concurrent
- Data volume

## Correlación con SM21
Gateway events también en SM21 (system log).

## Tunneled RFCs (secure)
Modern: SAP Cloud Connector, secure network communications (SNC).

- Kerberos or X.509 client cert
- No RFC over plain TCP

## Autorización
- `S_TCODE = SMGW`
- `S_ADMI_FCD = ST0R` — system admin

## Related transactions
- `SM59` — RFC destinations
- `SM21` — system log
- `RZ11` — parameters

title: SAP: performance tools — ST12 / SAT / SE30
tags: sap, st12, sat, se30, runtime analysis, trace
excerpt: Profilers para diagnostico de performance ABAP.
body:
## Herramientas y cuándo usar

### ST12 (recomendado hoy)
Unified trace: SQL + ABAP + memoria + RFC.

### SAT (successor de SE30)
Runtime analysis del programa ABAP.

### SE30 (legacy)
Runtime analysis viejo. SAT lo reemplaza.

### ST05 — SQL trace only
Cubierto en artículo separado.

## ST12 — SAP Trace Analysis
### Uso
1. `ST12` → new trace:
   - **Trace type**: Transaction, User, Work process
   - **Duration**: 60s típico
2. **Activate trace**
3. User o session ejecuta el proceso lento
4. Trace auto-stops after duration
5. `ST12 → Trace list → seleccionar` → analyze

### Vistas
- **Overview** — hot spots (top-consuming methods/statements)
- **ABAP trace** — call stack ABAP
- **DB trace** — SQL statements con tiempo
- **Memory** — allocations

## SAT (Runtime Analysis)
### Uso
1. `SAT`
2. **Variant**: DEFAULT o custom (define qué medir)
3. Botón **Execute** → seleccionar 'Transaction' + t-code
4. SAP runs con trace habilitado
5. Al terminar → auto-shows analysis

### Analysis views
- **Hit list** — statements con más tiempo
- **Calling hierarchy** — call stack
- **Statements** — línea por línea
- **Statistics** — summary

## Ejemplo caso

### 'MM03 tarda 30 segundos'
1. ST12 → activate trace filter para user `JPEREZ`, transaction `MM03`
2. JPEREZ ejecuta MM03 con material X
3. Trace stops
4. Analyze:
   - **Overview** → 25 seg consumidos por `SELECT * FROM MARC WHERE MATNR = X`
   - **DB trace** → esa SELECT devuelve 500,000 rows (all plants) — user solo necesita 1 plant
5. Fix: ABAP developer agrega `WHERE WERKS = <plant>` al SELECT → next run: 0.5 seg

## Filter trace
Avoid tracing everything (heavy overhead):
- Filter by user
- Filter by transaction
- Filter by program name
- Filter by include

## ST05 vs ST12 comparison
| Feature | ST05 | ST12 |
|---|---|---|
| SQL trace | ✓ | ✓ (uses ST05 under hood) |
| ABAP trace | ✗ | ✓ |
| Memory trace | ✗ | ✓ |
| RFC trace | Limited | ✓ |
| Filter | Basic | Rich |
| Aggregate | ✗ | ✓ |

## Overhead
Traces cost performance while active:
- 5-20% CPU overhead
- Storage per trace: MB

Nunca dejar habilitado permanentemente.

## Save trace file
- **Save** — permanent en DB (until purged)
- **Download** — save local .DAT file
- **Compare** — compare 2 traces

## Interpretation tips
### High DB time
- Missing index
- Full table scan
- Bulk operations un-batched

### High CPU time (ABAP)
- Nested loops without proper indexing
- String operations en loops
- ABAP without FOR ALL ENTRIES en table access

### High memory
- Large internal tables
- Not clearing tables between iterations
- ABAP dumps si excede limits

### High RFC time
- Chatty communication (many small calls)
- Batch calls (send array in 1 RFC)
- Network latency

## Retention
Traces auto-purge after 90 days default. Config:
- Params `abap/max_size_bytes_for_run_time_trace`

## SAP Notes
- 1786775 — ST12 setup
- 1671165 — trace analysis best practices

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` — trace tools
- `S_ADMI_FCD = ST0R` — trace admin

## S/4HANA + HANA
HANA tiene su propio profiler:
- `HANA studio → Performance → Load` — visual
- Or `M_EXPENSIVE_STATEMENTS` view
- Combine SAT (ABAP side) + HANA profiler (DB side) para full picture.

title: SAP: TCODE — creación de transacción custom
tags: sap, se93, tcode, transaction, custom
excerpt: Crear código de transacción para tu programa custom.
body:
## Uso
`SE93` — transaction maintenance.

## Create tcode
1. `SE93` → tcode name (must start with `Z` o `Y`): `ZMI_REPORT`
2. **Create**
3. **Description**: Reporte mensual XYZ
4. **Transaction type**:
   - **Dialog transaction** — call screen/program directly
   - **Report transaction** — call ABAP report (con optional variant)
   - **Parameter transaction** — pre-fill selection screen fields
   - **Variant transaction** — call transaction with fixed variant
   - **Method of a class transaction**
   - **Web Dynpro / OO Transaction**

### Report transaction (most common)
1. Report program: `ZMI_REPORT` (your ABAP program)
2. Screen number: 1000 (default screen para selection)
3. **Skip initial screen** checkbox: si querés que arranque directo (peligroso — no user parameters)

### Parameter transaction
Pre-fill selection screen with values:
1. Base transaction: `SU01`
2. **Default values** table:
   - Field: `BNAME` (username)
   - Default value: `JPEREZ`
3. Al usar el custom tcode → SU01 abre con JPEREZ already filled

### Variant transaction
Base transaction + fixed variant:
1. Base: `SE38`
2. Program: `RFITEMAP`
3. Variant: `Z_MENSUAL`

El user solo ve el resultado — no puede cambiar parametros.

## Auth check
Cada custom tcode chequea `S_TCODE` con el TCODE name. Agregar al role en PFCG.

### Additional auth (optional)
SE93 → **Auth object** field: forzar check adicional.

Ejemplo: tcode `ZDELETE_DATA` → require object `S_TABU_DIS` with special value.

## Save
Asigna transport request.

## Test
SAP command line: `/nZMI_REPORT` → debe abrir tu report.

## GUI menu
Agregar al menú del user:
- **PFCG** → tab **Menu** → **Transaction** → `ZMI_REPORT`
- Users con este role verán el tcode en su tree menu

## Icons
SE93 → **Icon** → assign an icon para menu.

## Delete
SE93 → transaction → **Delete**. 

Roles y transports references break — verificar antes.

## Common issues

### 'Program XXX does not exist'
Program name misspelled or not activated.

### 'No authorization for transaction ZMI_REPORT'
User doesn't have `S_TCODE = ZMI_REPORT` en su role.

### 'Screen 1000 not defined'
Program doesn't have screen 1000. Use screen 100 or check program dynpro list.

## Convert reports to tcode
Users rarely execute programs via SE38 directly. Custom tcode makes:
- Easier access
- Menu integration
- Authorization control granular

### Naming convention
- **Z*** — custom recomendado
- **Y*** — alternate custom namespace
- Numeric prefix common: `ZFI_01_REPORT`

## Enterprise namespace
Big companies register own namespace with SAP (e.g., `/EMPRESA/`).

Commonly `/EMP/*` for enterprise objects.

## Auth pattern for tcode
Restrict tcode + specific auth:

### PFCG example
Role `Z_MM_REPORTS`:
- `S_TCODE = ZMI_REPORT`
- `M_MSEG_LGO` limited to plant 1000

User can execute ZMI_REPORT but data restricted.

## Multi-tenant
Algunos tcodes se comportan según client (mandante). Custom tcodes must be tested en cada client if config differs.

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` — create tcode
- `S_TRANSPRT` — transport

title: SAP: SPAD — spool administration
tags: sap, spad, spool, printer, output device
excerpt: Config central de printers y access methods.
body:
## Uso
`SPAD` — Spool Administration.

### Tabs
- **Devices/Servers**
- **Device types**
- **Character sets**
- **Full administration**

## Devices (printers)
**Devices/Servers → Devices** → lista:
- Short name (ej: `HP01`)
- Device type (driver)
- Location
- Access method
- Host printer name
- Spool server

## Access methods (cómo llegar al printer)
- **L** — Local (SAP server prints directly to attached printer)
- **S** — SAPlpd (Windows spooler mediator)
- **C** — Direct OS spool via lpd/cups
- **U** — Remote via CUPS/LPD
- **E** — External OS command
- **G** — Frontend printing (impresora local del user)
- **X** — SAP Print Services (moderno)

## Add nuevo printer
1. `SPAD` → **Devices** → **Change**
2. **Create** button
3. Fields:
   - **Short name**: `HP01`
   - **Long name**: `HP LaserJet planta 1`
   - **Device type**: `HPLJIIID` (buscar F4)
   - **Spool server**: `sapserver_PRD_00` (donde reside)
   - **Access method**: `S` (SAPlpd, standard windows)
   - **Host printer**: `\\printserver\HP01` (Windows share)
4. Save

### Test
**Test print** button — send test page.

## Device types
Driver que sabe cómo formatear output para ese printer model:
- `HPLJIIID` — HP LaserJet III
- `SAPWIN` — generic Windows
- `SWINCF` — Windows con Cyrillic
- `SLPS` — PostScript

Algunos custom: SAP ships hundreds, plus per country.

## Frontend printing (G)
Imprime al printer default del user en su PC:
- Requires SAP GUI
- Access method G en el device SP01_DUMP or SWIN
- User no puede seleccionar otro printer — usa su default

## Ver stats
`SPAD → Devices/Servers → Devices` → click device → **Statistics**:
- Jobs printed
- Errors
- Last activity

## Ver spool queue
`SP01` — spool requests browse.
O `SPAD → Devices/Servers → Full administration → Devices → seleccionar → Contents`.

## Reroute prints
If printer HP01 broken, redirect all its queue to HP02:

### Manual
SP01 → filter by HP01 → select → **Change output device** → HP02 → Print.

### Config
SPAD → HP01 → **Change** → agregar 'Alt device' HP02.

## Delete spool requests
`SP01` con status filter → delete.

Or auto-cleanup con job `RSPO0041` (or `RSPO1041`) — scheduled.

## Retention
Default: 8 días.

Config en `SPAD → Extras → Configuration → Retention period`.

## PDF output
Device type `PDF1`:
- Access method: whatever
- Al 'print' a PDF1 → genera PDF en SAP inbox del user
- Descargar via SBWP o attach a email

## Common issues

### 'Access denied to printer'
- Printer configured en Windows print server but SAP user (or SIDadm on OS) doesn't have permission
- Grant NTFS/share permission a SIDadm account

### 'Printer not found'
- DNS resolution failure
- Print server down
- IP changed

### 'Character set mismatch'
- Spanish chars printing as ??? or garbage
- Wrong device type — use one with Latin-1 or Unicode support

### 'Spool request cancelled'
- OS-level issue: printer offline, out of paper
- Retry after fixing physical printer

## SP12 — TemSe consistency
`SP12 → TemSe database → Consistency check`.

Runs periodic to catch orphans.

## Frontend printing config
User sap gui → Options → **Printing** → default local printer.

Or via GPO — pre-configure defaults.

## Autorización
- `S_ADMI_FCD = SPAD` — SPAD admin
- `S_SPO_ACT` — action on spool
- `S_SPO_DEV` — device permission (per printer)
